summary: Paige quit. On Sep 2 at 11:17 she wrote 'hey!! i just wanted to inform that i’m leaving the agency tomorrow! thank you for what you have been doing but its just not working for me I’m sorry! i appreciate the time support and help x'. Four consecutive reports called this exact outcome — a quiet referral client who never complains, absorbing failure after failure — and it landed in week 10. The five days before she quit are the whole case file. What ALTR asked of her: Vivek's 'need login code' (Aug 28), 'Drop the logins' (Aug 29) and 'Need approval for the account' (Aug 30) — the sixth and seventh credential asks of the relationship, producing a SIXTH plaintext password post in the group chat ('this is @xpaigex18 / [REDACTED-PASSWORD]', Aug 29); Mayson's Aug 30 content quota, 'keep it topped up with 7 reels a week so 30 in total per month'; Mica's Aug 31 reappearance after 18 days of silence, not with reel inspo but with a lecture — 'just wanted to reiterate how important consistent posting is' — to a client whose Instagram had been locked four times in 30 days; and Stephski's Sep 1 invoice carrying 'please pay within 7 days to avoid any pausing of work'. What ALTR delivered her: nothing. The Aug 26 lockout was never closed — Vivek's final message on this account, Aug 30, is another request from her, and she never replied. Then on Aug 31 she raised a brand-new and serious problem: 'ive got a leak. someone using my stuff on a swingers website x'. Michelle answered 'send me the link of this babes and we will take care of it' — her first message in 44 days — Paige supplied the URL at 03:59 on Sep 1, and nobody has said a single word about it since. Nick (DMCA), the dedicated takedown owner, was never brought in despite a DMCA topic existing in this chat since day one. Her last request to ALTR went unanswered, and roughly 31 hours later she left. The only reply to the churn notice came 72 minutes later from Mayson, a chatter: 'Hey Paige would you like to hop on a call today and go over it?'. As of the close of this window — 46 hours after she gave notice — Derrek has not said anything.

health.rationale: Down 38 from 48. The client gave notice of termination on Sep 2; there is no lower-severity way to score a week. The 82 -> 66 -> 57 -> 48 -> 10 slide was continuous, entirely ALTR-caused, and flagged in writing every single week: the Aug 21 file predicted a fourth Instagram episode would be the escalation trigger, the Aug 28 file said 'an unstaffed relationship at week 10 is how a quiet referral client churns without ever complaining'. Both came true. Not one carry-forward item was closed this week: the Aug 26 lockout is 9 days open and Vivek's last act was to ask her for something else; the security remediation is 32 days old and gained a sixth plaintext credential post; Derrek's 'plenty of updates starting next week' is 34 days and five report weeks silent; Mica's 1-on-1 is 60 days unbooked. Meanwhile the week's outbound traffic was three credential demands, a 30-reels-a-month content quota, a posting-consistency lecture and an invoice with a work-pause clause — four asks and zero deliverables — and her one new request, a content leak on a swingers site, was left unanswered for the 53 hours between her posting the URL and the end of this window. The only points left on the board are that she exited without hostility ('i appreciate the time support and help x'), the notice period is 'tomorrow' rather than immediate, and Mayson offered a call inside 72 minutes. A save is still technically live, which is the only reason this is not lower.
